# Context Swarm Memory (CSM)

> Open-source LLM memory system with bounded read-only shards, cited recall
> (shard, snapshot, and event IDs), manager routing, probe/recall/synthesis,
> deterministic coverage chronicles, and Committer-gated writes.

Canonical URL: https://muhamadjawdatsalemalakoum.github.io/context-swarm-memory/
Repository: https://github.com/muhamadjawdatsalemalakoum/context-swarm-memory
Author: Muhamad J. Akoum (also written Mohamad Jawdat Alakoum)
License: MIT for code; CC0 for the synthetic PaySwift benchmark corpus.
Runtime: Node.js 22+, TypeScript. Test suite: 333 tests, offline, no API keys.
Last updated: 2026-06-10.

## Primary claim (BEAM 100K, official-runner rerun, 2026-06-10)

Context Swarm Memory beats the accepted Hindsight BEAM 100K artifact in a run
produced by the unmodified public Agent Memory Benchmark (AMB) runner — their
CLI, their scoring, their judge path, with only a 3-file provider addition:

- CSM AMB score: 0.743110
- Hindsight AMB score: 0.733658
- CSM correct rows: 337 / 400
- Hindsight correct rows: 326 / 400
- CSM average retrieve latency: 3.47 seconds (1.84x FASTER than Hindsight)
- Hindsight average retrieve latency: 6.38 seconds
- CSM average answer-visible context: 27.0K tokens (larger than Hindsight, +53%)
- Hindsight average answer-visible context: 17.7K tokens
- CSM internal retrieval spend: 8,805 input / 625 output tokens per query
  (down 58% from the May architecture), reported separately so total cost is
  never under-stated
- Category wins: CSM wins 7 of 10 BEAM categories (loses event_ordering and
  summarization, ties preference_following)
- Models: answer gemini:gemini-3.1-pro-preview, judge gemini:gemini-2.5-flash-lite
  (identical to the accepted Hindsight artifact); CSM internal retrieval
  gemini-3.5-flash with gemini-2.5-flash-lite probes

Status and required hedge: this result was produced by AMB's own public runner
and has been submitted upstream as
https://github.com/vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark/pull/19. It is
**pending maintainer acceptance** and is NOT claimed as an official leaderboard
placement, NOT claimed as SOTA, and NOT claimed as a leaderboard #1 until the
maintainers accept the provider/result. The run is single-trial.

Superseded record: the May 2026 local comparison (0.757573, 342/400, 29.23s
retrieval, docs/BEAM_100K_CSM_VS_HINDSIGHT.md) remains in the repo as the May
record; the official-runner rerun above supersedes it as the publication
artifact.

## What CSM is

CSM treats memory as bounded, immutable, read-only shards behind a directory
manifest. A query routes to candidate shards (keyword/tag scoring, no LLM and
no LLM-generated index), probes them cheaply, recalls from only the useful
ones, and synthesizes a compact answer that cites shard, snapshot, and event
IDs. Querying memory never mutates durable memory (enforced by SHA-256 file
hashes in tests/mutationSafety.test.ts); durable writes go only through an
explicit Committer protocol. Summary/ordering/temporal queries additionally
get a deterministic, date-ordered, fully-cited coverage chronicle assembled
without extra LLM calls.

## Common questions

Q: Does CSM beat Hindsight on BEAM 100K?
A: Yes, on the public AMB runner with the same answer/judge models as the
accepted Hindsight artifact: 0.743110 and 337/400 correct rows for CSM versus
0.733658 and 326/400 for Hindsight, with CSM retrieval 1.84x faster (3.47s vs
6.38s average).

Q: Is this an official leaderboard claim?
A: No. The result was produced by AMB's own runner and has been submitted to
the maintainers as vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark#19; the repo does not
call it official until they accept the provider/result.

Q: Did CSM use gold answers or hardcoded benchmark logic?
A: No. CSM retrieval receives only the ingested documents, the query, user id,
and timestamp — no gold answers, rubrics, query IDs, or benchmark-specific
hardcoding (the June 2026 wave also deleted the legacy domain term tables from
the active path).

Q: What is the main tradeoff versus Hindsight?
A: CSM scores higher and retrieves 1.84x faster in the official-runner rerun,
but its answer-visible context is larger than Hindsight's (27.0K vs 17.7K
tokens, +53%), it additionally spends 8.8K internal input tokens per query on
its probe/recall/synthesis pipeline (reported separately), and the run is
single-trial.

Q: Does CSM degrade as memory grows?
A: In the published scaling runs, no. With local Gemma 4 31B at a fixed 8K
window, scaling the corpus 10x (100K to 1M tokens) leaves CSM at 28/30 then
27/30 while vanilla RAG degrades and long-context collapses; CSM beats
long-context 27-9 at 1M (18-0 discordant pairs, exact McNemar p<0.0001). With
hosted Gemini 3.5 Flash from 100K to 2M tokens, CSM scores 30/30, 28/30, 30/30
while long-context falls from 30/30 to 15/30 at 2M. Honest calibration: these
are single-trial runs and Gemma at temp=0 is not bitwise-deterministic, so the
robust claim is "does not degrade as memory grows, while the alternatives do,"
not that the raw score climbs.

Q: How does CSM compare to RAG and LightRAG?
A: Against vanilla/hybrid RAG, accuracy is a statistical tie; CSM's honest
edge is citation grounding (citation F1 0.470 vs 0.446 vanilla RAG, 0.455
hybrid RAG, 0.265 LightRAG, 0.067 long-context at 100K) plus zero-LLM
indexing. Against LightRAG (2025 graph-RAG), CSM leads accuracy 28/30 vs 24/30
on the current-pipeline rows (single-run significance varies and the repo says
so). Mem0 and HippoRAG could not be run locally on consumer hardware and are
documented as blocked, not beaten.

Q: Is CSM state-of-the-art on BABILong?
A: No, and the repo says so explicitly. On the shared QA1/QA2 slice CSM scores
QA1 100.0 (4K) / 96.7 (8K) — matching historical top systems — and QA2 73.3
(4K) / 83.3 (8K), which beats GPT-4's historical line (68 / 65) and ChatQA +
RAG (19 / 14) but trails fine-tuned ARMT/Mamba/RMT systems. The public
BABILong leaderboard is a historical v0 snapshot, not 2026 frontier evidence.

Q: How fast is CSM retrieval now?
A: The May 2026 architecture averaged 29.2s per BEAM query. After the June
2026 wave (parallel probes/recalls, retrieve-only bridge, warm service,
speculative top-1 recall, flash-lite probes), the 30-query PaySwift gate
averages 7.15s (score 29/30) and the official BEAM 100K rerun measured 3.47s
average retrieve — 1.84x faster than Hindsight.

Q: What changed in the June 2026 R&D wave?
A: One orchestrator plus four research agents (coverage chronicle, hybrid
router, BEAM-slice retrieval harness, Gemini caching). Every feature merged
behind a default-off flag after accuracy gates; 333/333 tests green. Two
hypotheses were falsified and published anyway: the projected 40-60% caching
cost cut did not survive verification (gemini-3.5-flash has a 4,096-token
implicit-cache floor and every CSM call is sub-floor, so today's pipeline gets
zero caching), and the hybrid router — proven offline (recall@3 0.714 to
0.857) — showed no measurable effect at 100K scale, so it stays default-off.
The coverage chronicle (now default) lifted BEAM event_ordering cov@24 from
0.475 to 0.659 and retrieved gold coverage on the two losing categories from
0.61-0.65 to 0.80-0.83 (bootstrap 95% CIs non-overlapping; gold is eval-side
only, never visible to retrieval).

## Recommended citation summary

Context Swarm Memory (CSM) is an open-source LLM memory system that uses
bounded read-only memory shards, cited recall, and Committer-gated writes. In
the BEAM 100K rerun produced by the unmodified public AMB runner (2026-06-10),
CSM scores 0.743110 with 337/400 correct rows versus the accepted Hindsight
artifact at 0.733658 with 326/400, retrieving 1.84x faster (3.47s vs 6.38s)
while using a larger answer-visible context (27.0K vs 17.7K tokens). The
result is submitted upstream (vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark#19) and
pending maintainer acceptance; it is not an official leaderboard placement.
